PHASE 0 — IMAGERY DIRECTION
Issue #325 · Epic #323

Four directions for social imagery, all showing the SAME post so the comparison isn't rigged: the full-circle note about "Notorious" — Duran Duran at Irvine Meadows in 1987, Nile Rodgers at the Pacific Amphitheatre in 2026.

All content is real archive data, not placeholder.

Size is Instagram's 1080x1350 (4:5). That's deliberate: it's the most demanding format, because the image carries the whole post there and captions have no clickable links. A direction that survives 4:5 will survive a 1200x630 link card.

Pick a direction (or a hybrid) and the next canvas expands it across all four channels, plus the nine-up grid and the timeline scroll.

Type is Playfair Display + Source Sans 3, lifted from the existing design system. Cultural-category violet #7c3aed is the same token og-image.ts already uses.

TRACK A — TYPOGRAPHIC / EDITORIAL

The hook is the entire image. Design-system ground, Playfair at 82px, category rule, venues and years as a footer.

Why it might win: nothing to license, nothing to break, no dead-image risk (#252, #315 simply don't exist here). Reads at feed scale. Cheapest to build — it's the solid-colour fallback already in og-image.ts, promoted to a primary treatment.

The tradeoff: austerity. This is the direction most at risk of feeling corporate rather than personal — a feed of type-on-colour can look like a SaaS changelog. Judge it in the nine-up grid, not here.

TRACK B — DATA-DERIVED GENERATIVE

The bars are the real archive: 184 shows per year, 1984-2026. 1987 and 2026 are lit; the dotted arc spans the 39 years between them.

Why it might win: wholly owned, unique to this archive, impossible to mistake for stock, and already on-brand — the site IS data visualisation. Every post generates a different shape from its own records, so the feed varies without anyone art-directing it. No licensing exposure at all.

The tradeoff: it needs a story with a shape. A one-off show with no span, no gap and no repeat has nothing to draw, so this can't be the only direction — it needs a fallback for thin posts.

TRACK C — MATERIAL / METAPHOR

Designed ticket stubs as original artwork — evoking the object, never a scan of one. The project's own metaphor is album liner notes, and the prose here literally ends on "it accumulated in my ticket stubs."

Why it might win: warmest of the four and the most obviously personal. Thematically exact. Owned outright. The light ground also breaks up a feed that would otherwise be uniformly dark.

The tradeoff: the most template-like. Two stubs works beautifully for a full-circle post and awkwardly for a post about one night — the furniture may not survive contact with the other 13 detectors.

TRACK D — LICENSED PHOTOGRAPHY

Shown with a deliberately marked placeholder. No real photo is embedded here, because embedding one is the exact risk under review — see the provenance policy, #327.

Why it might win: photography outperforms graphics on Instagram, and it's the only direction that puts a human face in the feed.

The tradeoff, and it's the heavy one: every image source we have (Google Places, Spotify album art, Cover Art Archive) is licensed for display on our own site, not for republication under a brand account. Spotify's guidelines specifically prohibit the overlay treatment. The risk isn't a lawsuit, it's an automated strike on an account with no goodwill to absorb it.

Note the caption line — CC-licensed sources need attribution, which costs a line of the design on every post forever.
